# Clade Reference: Symbolic Line — v0.3

*Working document. Do not cite externally.*

## How to read this document

Each entry covers one cell of the symbolic line in the ABHOP framework. Venn labels (motivations, tendencies, signatures, capacities, breakthrough) are pulled verbatim from *Inheritance Lines v3.0* and must not be paraphrased. The constituent-human framing names the individual parameterized by collective context, not the collective itself; the collective is symbolic-fauna, the personality traits are symbolic-flora.

**Traceability marks:**

- **HIGH** — full APA confirmed in Smithers extraction or SQLite cache; wording verified
- **MODERATE** — partial details or reconstructed from extraction text; APA not fully confirmed
- **LOW** — secondary source or unverified chain
- **[INFERRED]** — no Smithers extraction source; general knowledge only

---

## Cell 1: Band-Human

**What the cell is.** A Band-Human is a human whose personality constellation is parameterized by band life: a mobile forager group of roughly 20–30 adults whose cohesion depends entirely on direct reciprocal exchange among individuals who are mostly not close genetic relatives. The breaking motivation at this cell is Commitment (Effector slot), which displaces Impetus — marking the neuronal-to-symbolic boundary and making reputation management the primary individual imperative. The collective this human inhabits is the band as meme-fauna; the personality traits expressed are symbolic-flora calibrated to band ecology.

**The milestone.** Speaking, the capacity for open-ended, combinatorially productive language that makes gossip, reputation tracking, and shared intentionality scalable beyond dyadic grooming ranges. The framework treats Speaking as the breakthrough that makes Commitment operationalizable at band scale, and treats Band-Human as defined by band ecology rather than by species. The date and species-spread of Speaking are an open empirical debate: the sapiens behavioral-modernity record (roughly 100 to 300 KYA) and the Neanderthal symbolic record both bear on it (see Dating and species below). The framework presents the debate and does not resolve it.

**Key references.**

Co-residence patterns in hunter-gatherer societies show unique human social structure. *Science*, *331*(6022), 1286–1289. | HIGH | Mean band size ~28 adults across 32 societies; co-residents are mostly genetically unrelated — establishes Commitment-over-kinship as the structural norm, not an exception |

**Fun specifics.**

- Hill et al. (2011) sampled 32 hunter-gatherer societies and found that median co-resident band members were mostly *not* close genetic relatives — cohesion runs on Commitment, not kinship alone, which makes the Effector slot shift from Impetus to Commitment structurally load-bearing rather than ornamental (Hill et al., 2011).
- Meat Pooling (Reactor capacity). A Ju/'hoansi or Aché hunter brings down a large animal once every few weeks at best. Most of the meat he kills is eaten by people other than himself. Kaplan and colleagues calculated that across a forager's lifetime, a hunter delivers roughly 40 to 60 percent of his calories to people other than his own household. This pattern only makes sense as part of a reciprocal accounting system that runs across decades and across the band: when his hunt fails, someone else's kill fills his bowl, and his children eat from the kills of older men whose children will later eat from his. Meat Pooling is the band's solution to the high variance of hunting: meat spoils, individual luck is unreliable, but the band's collective table is more stable than any single hunter's. The Reactor capacity at this cell is the action-and-revision of accumulation and redistribution, coordinated across the group without anyone running the system from the top.
  - *Citation.* Kaplan, Hill, Lancaster, & Hurtado 2000 Evolutionary Anthropology 9:156
  - *Repeats.* Unique to Band. (Conquering at Empire is the structurally-inverted sibling at the same Reactor class slot, different cell — pooling becomes seizing.)
- Collaborative Fission (Conservator capacity) is not merely a kinship nicety: Walker et al. (2010) document reciprocal exogamy systems that systematically extend coalition radius beyond any single band's fighting strength — reproductive exchange as political alliance infrastructure.
- Blombos Cave preserves a cross-hatch drawing on silcrete at 73 KYA (Henshilwood et al., 2018) and engraved geometric ochre pieces at 75–100 KYA (Henshilwood et al., 2009); both predate any verbal record of Speaking, making material traces the only chronological anchor for the breakthrough.
- Self-Reference (Connector signature) implies the band-level individual can hold a stable representation of how *others* represent *them* — the cognitive groundwork for shame, pride, and reputation monitoring; all three self-conscious emotions presuppose a theory of mind that models one's own model of oneself. [INFERRED — no Smithers extraction covers Cooley, Tangney, Tracy & Robins, or Hofstadter directly]
- Alloparenting (Pursuer capacity). Hadza foragers do something other great apes don't: hand their infants around. In the first weeks of life, a Hadza infant is held by an average of about fourteen different caregivers. Older siblings, aunts, grandmothers, unrelated band members — all rotate through. Sarah Hrdy argued that human cooperative breeding is so distinctive from the rest of the great-ape pattern (where infants stay almost exclusively with the mother for years) that our cognitive capacities for reading minds and building trust evolved partly to support it. The shared-childcare arrangement requires constant tracking of who can be trusted with a child and who will reciprocate. Alloparenting is goal-pursuit (raising the child) using affiliation (network) and autonomy (judgment about competence) without the kind of fixed kinship structures that come later.
  - *Citation.* Hrdy 2009 Mothers and Others; Crittenden & Marlowe 2008 Human Nature 19:249 for Hadza alloparenting empirical data
  - *Repeats.* Same capacity at Settlement, different social structure. Band case is forager-band cooperative breeding with rotating non-relative alloparents; Settlement case is structured extended-family alloparenting with consistent grandmother roles
- Reputation (Controller capacity). Polly Wiessner spent decades documenting Ju/'hoansi forager conversation. Daytime conversation among the Ju/'hoansi is largely practical: where to hunt, who is sick, what to fetch. At night around the fire, the conversation shifts — most night-talk turns out to be stories and gossip about people who are absent. Wiessner argued the night-fire was where reputations were tracked, repaired, ridiculed, and assigned: the band's social ledger updated by people talking about people not in the room. Without language, this kind of indirect reputation tracking is not possible. With language, a band of thirty people can keep track of everyone's standing in everyone else's eyes, even people who are away from the fire that night. Reputation at this cell is the linguistically-mediated version that gossip and indirect transmission make scalable.
  - *Citation.* Wiessner 2014 PNAS 111:14027 "Embers of society: Firelight talk among the Ju/'hoansi Bushmen"
  - *Repeats.* Same capacity at Primate, different organism. Primate case is direct social-comparison tracking in capuchins (Brosnan & de Waal 2003); Band case is linguistic indirect reputation — tracking standing through speech about absent third parties

**Smithers coverage.** MODERATE-to-HIGH for forager ecology. The Innovations field reconnaissance extraction (Block 2) covers band size, meat pooling, and intergroup marriage with full APA for Hill et al. (2011) and Kaplan et al. (2000) and partial confirmation for Walker et al. (2010). Block 4 provides Henshilwood et al. (2018) at HIGH and (2009) at MODERATE. ABSENT for the Self-Reference / self-conscious emotion cluster (Cooley, Tangney, Tracy & Robins, Hofstadter) — all [INFERRED] — and for the gossip literature (Dunbar) and Boehm's reverse-dominance hierarchy work.

**Dating and species (open, by framework decision).** The symbolic record is split across hominins. Sapiens behavioral-modernity markers cluster around 100 to 300 KYA (Blombos abstract marks and ochre, the modernity package). Neanderthal symbolic behavior flanks or predates this: shell ornaments around 115 KYA (Hoffmann et al. 2018), Iberian cave art older than 64.8 KYA (Hoffmann et al. 2018), Bruniquel Cave ring structures at 176.5 KYA (Jaubert et al. 2016). The framework treats Band-Human as ecology-defined and Speaking as a capacity whose horizon and species-spread are contested; it presents both records and does not adjudicate sapiens-specific versus genus-level. The strong form of sapiens symbolic uniqueness is not defensible on current evidence.

## Cell 2: Settlement-Human

**What the cell is.** A Settlement-Human is a human whose personality constellation is parameterized by sedentary village life: a fixed-location community whose cohesion depends on accumulation, storage, and recurring structured obligation rather than mobile reciprocal exchange. The breaking motivation at this cell is Stability (Regulator slot), which displaces Mastery — shifting the individual's primary orientation from skill-demonstration to consistent rule-following across seasons. The collective this human inhabits is the settlement as a norm-generating superorganism; the personality traits expressed are symbolic-flora calibrated to sedentary agricultural ecology.

**The milestone.** Common Knowledge — synchronized cross-stranger mutual awareness in the Pinker / Lewis / Schiffer sense, where each party knows that the others know, and knows that they know that they know, scaled across strangers by the durable public focal points settlement architecture introduces (town squares, monuments, marketplaces). The breakthrough position names this cognitive achievement because it is the more fundamental one: norms presuppose common knowledge (Bicchieri) and sit one slot out as the Conservator capacity, not the breakthrough. The Neolithic Revolution provides the archaeological anchor: cultivation begins in the Fertile Crescent ~11,700–10,200 BP; Çatalhöyük (~9,500–7,700 BP) represents a large sedentary agglomeration without clear hierarchy, operating on normative coordination alone. [Milestone dating [INFERRED] — no Smithers extraction covers Neolithic archaeology directly.]

**Key references.**

| Citation | Traceability | Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| Roberts, B. W. (2006). Continuity and change in personality from childhood to adulthood. In D. K. Mroczek & T. D. Little (Eds.), *Handbook of personality development* (pp. 51–70). Lawrence Erlbaum Associates. | MODERATE | Social Investment Principle: adult role commitment creates environmental press for Conscientiousness crystallization — mechanism for why Settlement-Human produces the Conscientiousness debut at the Effector×Regulator Controller slot |
| Roberts, B. W., Kuncel, N. R., Shiner, R., Caspi, A., & Goldberg, L. R. (2007). The power of personality: The comparative validity of personality traits, socioeconomic status, and cognitive ability for predicting important life outcomes. *Perspectives on Psychological Science*, *2*(4), 313–345. | MODERATE | Conscientiousness predicts mortality r=.09, larger than SES (r=.02) or IQ (r=.06); approximately 7 additional years of life expectancy — quantifies the survival stakes of the Conscientiousness slot in agricultural context |
| Roberts, B. W., Jackson, J. J., Fayard, J. V., Edmonds, G., & Meints, J. (2012). Conscientiousness. In M. R. Leary & R. H. Hoyle (Eds.), *Handbook of individual differences in social behavior* (pp. 369–381). Guilford Press. | MODERATE | Industriousness (sustained effort toward goals) vs. Orderliness (routine maintenance of environment) bifurcation within Conscientiousness; maps onto Farming (Reactor) vs. Householding distinction |
| Stephan, Y., Sutin, A. R., & Terracciano, A. (2018). Subjective age and personality development: A 10-year study. *Journal of Personality*, *86*(3), 413–423. | MODERATE | Industriousness facet predicts longevity (~25% lower mortality per SD); self-control facet does not — facet-level specificity relevant to the agricultural-commitment interpretation |

**Fun specifics.**

- Norms (Conservator capacity). Çatalhöyük (~9,500–7,700 BP) housed up to 8,000 people with no evident palace, temple, or elite burial; every house is the same size and entered through the roof, making architectural equality literally structurally enforced. The settlement ran on shared behavioral expectations rather than hierarchy — the coordination logic the Conservator slot at this cell names. [INFERRED — no Smithers extraction covers Çatalhöyük]
- Roberts et al. (2007) show that Conscientiousness predicts survival outcomes more strongly than IQ (r=.06) or socioeconomic status (r=.02); in a sedentary agricultural setting where stored food is the margin between survival and starvation across seasons, the individual who shows up reliably to plant, weed, and harvest has a categorical adaptive advantage over the skilled improviser (Roberts et al., 2007).
- Roberts et al. (2012) show that Conscientiousness bifurcates into Industriousness (keep working) and Orderliness (keep things in their place); the settlement household requires both facets in a way band foraging does not — crops do not wait for the hunter to feel ready, and grain stores require systematic maintenance.
- Self-Construal (Operator signature, debut at Settlement-Human) captures the independent-to-interdependent dimension of self-representation; the shift from Band-Human's Sociometer to Settlement-Human's Self-Construal marks the cultural individuation/embeddedness axis becoming salient as fixed property rights and household boundaries create the first stable structures around which independent vs. embedded selfhood can take shape. The kind of farming, not just farming itself, shapes which way self-construal settles: Talhelm et al. (2014, Science 344:603–608) find that a history of paddy-rice agriculture, with its coordinated labor and shared irrigation at roughly twice the labor of wheat, makes cultures more interdependent, while dry, rain-fed wheat farming makes them more independent. The difference holds along the within-China rice-wheat border after controlling for climate and wealth. Kitayama (of Markus & Kitayama) is a co-author, so the study operationalizes the same independent/interdependent dimension. [Rice Theory: ‡ web-verified, pending Smithers ingest. Markus & Kitayama and Triandis framing: INFERRED, no Smithers extraction.]
- Farming (Reactor capacity) is the structural inversion of Meat Pooling: foragers share meat because it spoils and because reciprocal sharing averages risk; settlers store grain because it keeps and because stored surplus is the founding act of unequal wealth accumulation — the same Effector Reactor slot, an inverted social logic. [INFERRED]
- Assertiveness (Regulator×Modeler Anticipator) at Settlement-Human functions as norm-negotiating rather than dominance-asserting: the settled farmer establishes position within a stable hierarchy through reliable performance and vocal claim-making, not open competition with strangers. [INFERRED — no extraction covers Assertiveness as distinct from Extraversion in this context]
- Wealth (Planner capacity). A hunter-gatherer band has no real wealth. The food spoils. Tools are simple and replicable. When someone dies, there is little to inherit. A settled village transforms this. Grain stores in clay jars sit through winter; herds of sheep are passed to children; land use rights are inherited. Borgerhoff Mulder and Bowles 2009 measured wealth inequality across 21 small-scale societies — foraging, horticultural, agricultural, pastoral. In foraging bands, inequality is low and unstable across generations: a rich family this generation is not predictive of the next. In farming and herding societies, the same families stay wealthy or stay poor for generations — wealth becomes a thing that exists and persists across time. The Settlement-Human's Planner runs on stored value in a way the Band-Human's didn't have material for.
  - *Citation.* Borgerhoff Mulder, Bowles, et al. 2009 Science 326:682 "Intergenerational wealth transmission and the dynamics of inequality in small-scale societies"
  - *Repeats.* Unique to Settlement
- Alloparenting (Pursuer capacity). When humans settled into agricultural villages, alloparenting became more structured. The mobile band pattern — many alloparents, lots of variation in who's around — gave way to extended-family households where the same grandmother might raise multiple grandchildren while her daughters worked the fields. Sear and Mace 2008 combined 45 studies of small-scale societies and found a consistent pattern: in farming societies, the presence of a maternal grandmother substantially improves a child's chances of survival to age five. Paternal grandmothers and other kin have smaller and more variable effects. Same alloparenting capacity as Band, channeled through fixed kinship structures rather than rotating band membership: known relatives, known houses, known seasonal labor demands. The alloparent is no longer "whoever is nearby" but "the specific aunt in the next room."
  - *Citation.* Sear & Mace 2008 Evolution and Human Behavior 29:1 "Who keeps children alive? A review of the effects of kin on child survival"
  - *Repeats.* Same capacity at Band, different social structure. Band case is rotating non-relative alloparents (Hadza); Settlement case is extended-family alloparenting with the grandmother effect

**Smithers coverage.** DENSE for the Conscientiousness psychology sub-cluster: the Conscientiousness source card covers Roberts (2006), Roberts et al. (2007), Roberts et al. (2012), and Stephan et al. (2018) at MODERATE traceability, providing functional grounding for the Controller debut. Self-Construal carries one web-verified anchor pending Smithers ingest (Talhelm et al. 2014, the Rice Theory), while the Markus & Kitayama and Triandis framing remains uncovered. ABSENT for Neolithic archaeology (Çatalhöyük, Göbekli Tepe, Fertile Crescent chronology) and Assertiveness as a distinct construct. A Settlement-Human book passage requires [INFERRED] scaffolding for its archaeological components and for the Markus & Kitayama / Triandis side of self-construal.

## Cell 3: City-Human

**What the cell is.** A City-Human is a human whose personality constellation is parameterized by urban life: a dense, occupationally differentiated settlement whose cohesion depends on legal codes, market exchange, and institutional representation rather than face-to-face normative pressure. The breaking motivation at this cell is Representation (Modeler slot), which replaces Autonomy; Affiliation persists. Representation shifts the individual's primary orientation toward being recognized within an institutional order that includes strangers. The collective this human inhabits is the city as a symbiosis of settlements and trade networks, making this the first symbiosis cell on the symbolic line; the personality traits expressed are symbolic-flora calibrated to urban anonymous ecology.

**The milestone.** Codes — written, portable, enforceable rule-sets that coordinate strangers who share no face-to-face norm-maintenance history. The Urban Revolution provides the archaeological anchor: Uruk (~5,500–5,000 BP), Mohenjo-daro (~4,500–3,900 BP), and contemporaneous Nile and Yellow River urban centers represent the first settlements large enough that codes rather than the face-to-face norms of settlement scale must bear the primary coordination load. [Milestone dating [INFERRED] — no Smithers extraction covers city archaeology directly.]

**Key references.**

| Citation | Traceability | Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| Judge, T. A., Locke, E. A., Durham, C. C., & Kluger, A. N. (1998). Dispositional effects on job and life satisfaction: The role of core evaluations. *Journal of Applied Psychology*, *83*(1), 17–34. | HIGH | Founding Core Self-Evaluations paper; Self-Evaluation (Connector signature, debut at City-Human) operationalized as self-esteem + generalized self-efficacy + locus of control + emotional stability |
| Judge, T. A., & Bono, J. E. (2001). Relationship of core self-evaluations traits — self-esteem, generalized self-efficacy, locus of control, and emotional stability — with job satisfaction and job performance: A meta-analysis. *Journal of Applied Psychology*, *86*(1), 80–92. | HIGH | Meta-analytic confirmation of the CSE cluster across 169 independent samples (N~59,000); ρ=.37 for job satisfaction, ρ=.23 for job performance |
| Judge, T. A., Bono, J. E., Erez, A., & Locke, E. A. (2005). Core self-evaluations and job and life satisfaction: The role of self-concordance and goal attainment. *Journal of Applied Psychology*, *90*(2), 257–268. | HIGH | CSE mediates outcome effects via goal self-concordance — maps onto city-scale occupational role structure where institutional position is the primary self-evaluation referent |
| Ashton, M. C., & Lee, K. (2007). Empirical, theoretical, and practical advantages of the HEXACO model of personality structure. *Personality and Social Psychology Review*, *11*(2), 150–166. | MODERATE | Righteousness (Adapter at City-Human, debut here before Integrity at Empire) framed within HEXACO Agreeableness vs. Honesty-Humility distinction; establishes the moral-emotions Adapter progression |

**Fun specifics.**

- The Sumerian cuneiform tablets at Uruk (~5,200 BP) are primarily accounting documents — lists of beer rations and grain allocations — not literature; the first writing is Codes, not poetry, and the first urban personality problem is who gets what from whom according to what enforceable rule. [INFERRED — no Smithers extraction covers Mesopotamian archaeology]
- Judge et al. (1998) define Core Self-Evaluations as a unitary higher-order construct binding self-esteem, generalized self-efficacy, locus of control, and emotional stability; in a city, all four collapse to a single question: can I hold my institutional position against strangers who are also competing for it? Self-Evaluation replaces Self-Reference because the reference group is now an institution, not a face-to-face band (Judge et al., 1998).
- Extraversion (Regulator×Modeler Anticipator, debut at City-Human) emerges structurally as the city creates an occupational ecology in which asserting oneself in front of strangers pays — the merchant, the lawyer, the priest, the soldier are all roles requiring social approach behavior with unrelated others, a context absent in bands and uncommon in settlements. [INFERRED for ecological correlate; trait debut from *Inheritance Lines v3.0*]
- Crime (Pursuer capacity). There is no organized crime in a forager band. In a group of thirty people who know each other from infancy, watch every action, and depend on each other for food, "stealing" doesn't compute as a sustained life strategy. The kid who takes someone else's spear is ridiculed and corrected within hours. The city changes this. Density creates anonymity; surplus creates targets; institutional complexity creates gaps. By imperial Rome, organized criminal bands called grassatores operated in the streets at night. Medieval cities developed thieves' guilds with their own internal hierarchies. Modern cities support everything from pickpocket networks to wire fraud to organized racketeering. Crime is the Pursuer capacity in its city-form: goal-pursuit without rule-enforced inhibition, made viable because the city created the structural conditions — strangers, surplus, gaps in oversight — under which code-violation pays.
  - *Citation.* Glaeser 2011 Triumph of the City for the urban-density-and-crime relationship; Sallust Bellum Catilinae on the grassatores of late Republican Rome; Geltner 2008 Medieval Prison on medieval urban crime structures
  - *Repeats.* Unique to City
- Judge & Bono (2001) meta-analyzed 169 independent samples and found CSE correlates ρ=.37 with job satisfaction across occupational contexts — city-scale life produces stable enough occupational roles that personality variation on the CSE cluster becomes a reliable predictor of whether an individual thrives within the institutional order or chafes against it (Judge & Bono, 2001).
- Righteousness (Adapter at City-Human) is the first appearance of a moral-identity trait in the Adapter slot: Agreeableness (cooperation toward the proximal known other) gives way to Righteousness (alignment with the city's codes as moral authority), marking the transition from relationship-maintenance to norm-internalization as the primary individual accommodation mechanism. [INFERRED for mechanism; label from *Inheritance Lines v3.0*]
- Distributing (Planner capacity). Cities solved a problem hunter-gatherers and small villages never had: what to do with the surplus that hundreds of thousands of people generate when they live in one place. The answer was distribution networks. Imperial Rome ran a system called the annona: grain ships from Egypt and North Africa unloaded at Ostia, were inventoried, transported up the Tiber, and distributed free to roughly 200,000 citizens at monthly distribution centers in the capital. The system required record-keeping, scheduling, transport coordination, contracts with shipowners, storage logistics, and political management — and it sustained the city of Rome for centuries. The Distributing capacity is strategic deliberation about how surplus moves through a network of people who don't know each other personally. Granaries, markets, redistribution, futures contracts, supply chains: all sit at this slot.
  - *Citation.* Erdkamp 2005 The Grain Market in the Roman Empire; Garnsey 1988 Famine and Food Supply in the Greco-Roman World
  - *Repeats.* Unique to City
- Farming (Reactor capacity). When cities exist, farming has to feed people who aren't farming. By 2000 BCE, irrigation networks in southern Mesopotamia fed cities of tens of thousands from grain grown in fields the urban consumers never saw. Robert Adams' archaeological work on the hinterland of Uruk showed organized canal networks reaching dozens of kilometers from the city core, all dedicated to feeding the urban population. The capacity is the same as the Settlement village's stored grain — accumulate, store, manage — but the scale is categorically different. The farmer is now feeding strangers a hundred kilometers away through a chain of intermediaries, granaries, and barge networks. The Settlement farmer fed her own household and village; the City farmer feeds an urban core through institutional infrastructure she may never see.
  - *Citation.* Adams 1981 Heartland of Cities; Pollock 1999 Ancient Mesopotamia for synthesis
  - *Repeats.* Same capacity at Settlement, different scale. Settlement case is village-scale grain storage and seasonal cultivation; City case is irrigation networks supporting urban populations through long-distance distribution
- Standardizing (Conservator capacity). A city of fifty thousand people needs standards. If everyone's "pound" is slightly different, trade gets paralyzing. The Mesopotamian solution was the silver shekel — a fixed weight of silver, held as a master standard at the temple, that buyers and sellers across the city used to measure everything else. The same logic produced the cubit (a fixed length, held physically as a master ruler), the Egyptian palm and digit, the standardized brick sizes in Mohenjo-daro and Harappa. The Conservator capacity at the City is the slow maintenance of these shared references — keeping the master weight intact, training inspectors, replacing damaged standards. Without standardization, a city of strangers can't trade at scale.
  - *Citation.* Powell 1971 (and later) work on Mesopotamian metrology; Kenoyer 1998 Ancient Cities of the Indus Valley Civilization for Indus standardization
  - *Repeats.* Same capacity at Empire, different territorial scope. City case is intra-city metrology (shekel, cubit, brick); Empire case is imperial-scale uniformity across territories that never meet
- Codes and the scale of cities. The City breakthrough is what lets coordination reach past face-to-face memory. A settlement coordinates people who watch each other; a city coordinates strangers through written, portable, enforceable rule. The cell's reinforcing cycle is the engine: records enable taxation, taxation funds specialists, and specialists produce more records. Four mechanisms carry the scaling. Standardized fungible tokens (currency, weights, measures, calendars) let value and obligation move system-wide without renegotiation. Standing records make a large population legible to a center, which is the precondition for governing at scale. Codified enforceable rules substitute for personal trust, which lets strangers transact and lets markets grow past the circle of people who know each other. The medium sets the reach: light portable codes extend control across space, and durable codes extend it across time.
  - The cross-line rhyme. Codes are to the city what mitochondria are to the eukaryote. Internal respiration broke the energetic ceiling that kept prokaryotes small, which bought the eukaryote a larger genome and greater complexity. Codes break the coordination ceiling that keeps settlements small, which buys the city a larger store of standing information and greater institutional complexity. The deeper rhyme runs from energy to information to scale: more energy per gene buys more genome, and more externalized record buys more coordination. Currency is the city's energy currency, a standardized token that decouples value from any single exchange the way the cell's energy token decouples power from any single reaction. The genetic-side construct is the Host, the eukaryote read as a chimera of host and incorporated symbiont (see `cybernetics_and_sentience`), and the City is the symbolic line's chimera of settlements and trade networks. The mitochondrial anchor is Lane's bioenergetics.
  - The scaling empirics. Cities scale like metabolizing organisms. Socioeconomic output rises superlinearly with population at an exponent near 1.15, and infrastructure rises sublinearly at an exponent near 0.83. The causal lever in that work is interaction density rather than codes. The framework's contribution is the missing half: codes are the standardizing infrastructure that converts more strangers into more coordinated interactions, which is what the scaling law measures. [framework, exposed; the bridge between the code-to-governance literature and the city-to-output literature is not drawn by existing theorists]
  - *Citation.* Innis, Empire and Communications (1950) and The Bias of Communication (1951) for medium and the reach of polities; Goody, The Logic of Writing and the Organization of Society (1986) for writing and administrative scale; Scott, Seeing Like a State (1998) and Against the Grain (2017) for legibility and the fiscal origin of writing; North, Institutions, Institutional Change and Economic Performance (1990) and Greif, Institutions and the Path to the Modern Economy (2006) for institutions and impersonal exchange; Hidalgo, Why Information Grows (2015) for information capacity and economic complexity; Bettencourt, Lobo, Helbing, Kuhnert and West (PNAS 2007) and Bettencourt (Science 2013) for urban scaling; Lane for mitochondrial bioenergetics. [Innis and the urban-scaling work web-cited 2026-06-15; the remainder are authorial lineage pending verification and Smithers ingest]
  - *Repeats.* Unique to City

**Smithers coverage.** MODERATE-HIGH for the Core Self-Evaluations cluster: Judge et al. (1998), Judge & Bono (2001), and Judge et al. (2005) are all confirmed at HIGH traceability in the SQLite cache (`papers` table), making Self-Evaluation (Connector) the best-documented structural element in this cell. ABSENT for city archaeology, urban scaling theory (West, Bettencourt), the anthropology of trade networks, Extraversion's ecological emergence story, and the structural sociology of Crime as a city-specific life strategy. The Extraversion debut has no extraction support beyond the *Inheritance Lines* framework label itself.

## Cell 4: Empire-Human

**What the cell is.** An Empire-Human is a human whose personality constellation is parameterized by imperial life: a multi-city polity whose cohesion depends on shared Stories — origin myths, sacred texts, ideological systems, and dynastic narratives — rather than face-to-face codes or norms. The breaking motivation at this cell is Universality (Reviser slot), which replaces Affiliation. Universality shifts the individual's primary orientation toward participation in a collective narrative that makes the empire's reach feel cosmically legitimate. The collective this human inhabits is the empire as a symbiosis of cities and colonial outposts; the personality traits expressed are symbolic-flora calibrated to an ecology where abstract identification with a vast, impersonal order is the primary individual survival problem.

**The milestone.** Trust — stranger-to-stranger reliance extended through universalizing frameworks (a shared faith, law, or ideology) that let people who will never meet rely on one another. The transmissible narratives that carry it are the Stories capacity one slot out; the breakthrough position names the reliance those narratives make possible. The Axial Age (~800–200 BCE) provides the clearest crystallization point: the near-simultaneous emergence of Confucianism, Buddhism, Greek philosophy, Zoroastrianism, and Second Temple Judaism across four independent civilizational cores each produce universal ethical frameworks capable of motivating strangers to rely on an imperial order beyond their immediate city-state. [Milestone dating [INFERRED] from general knowledge and Jaspers (1949); no Smithers extraction covers the Axial Age directly.]

**Fun specifics.**

- De Raad et al. (2010) compared 14 personality taxonomies across 12 language groups and found only three factors replicate with high congruence: Dynamism (Extraversion-like), Affiliation (Agreeableness-like), and Order (Conscientiousness-like); Openness-to-Experience failed to replicate — exactly what the framework predicts if Intellect is a late-arriving trait whose ecological conditions (scribal culture, philosophical inquiry, multi-civilization contact) only assemble at imperial scale (De Raad et al., 2010).
- Assmann & Czaplicka (1995) distinguish *communicative memory* (living conversation, ~80-year horizon, biographical and personal) from *cultural memory* (sacred texts, rituals, monuments, multi-generational and institutionally maintained); the Trust breakthrough is precisely this transition — empire cohesion requires cultural memory because the empire outlasts any communicative chain (Assmann & Czaplicka, 1995).
- Ashton & Lee (2016) report that Honesty-Humility increases approximately 1 SD from age 18 to 60 in a sample of N~97,583 — Integrity is a late-life crystallization within individual development, consistent with its position as the most structurally recent Adapter slot on the symbolic line. [Ashton & Lee 2016 cited from HEXACO source card; full APA not confirmed — MODERATE]
- Identity (Operator signature, debut at Empire-Human) replaces Self-Construal: the individual is no longer navigating independent vs. interdependent self-representation relative to a known community but identifying themselves as Roman, Han, Muslim, or Brahmin — categories that are cosmological rather than face-to-face; the referent community is imagined and the self-label is imperial. [INFERRED for mechanism; label from *Inheritance Lines v3.0*]
- Conquering (Reactor capacity). In 80 years, the Mongols conquered roughly a quarter of the world's land surface. They began as a confederation of steppe tribes under Genghis Khan in 1206 and reached the gates of Vienna by the 1240s. Their method was the structural inversion of forager risk-pooling. Where a band of hunters distributed calories to average risk across people, the Mongol horde concentrated everything — grain, livestock, gold, captives, artisans — at the imperial center. Imperial conquest is the Reactor capacity in its empire-form: the same action-regulation-revision triad as Meat Pooling, the same Reactor slot, but with the social logic inverted. Pooling becomes hoarding. Distribution becomes extraction. Sharing becomes seizure. From Akkad (~2334 BCE) onward, every large empire has run some version of this Reactor: accumulation by absorbing what's already been accumulated elsewhere.
  - *Citation.* Allsen 1987 Mongol Imperialism and the Policies of the Grand Qan Möngke or May 2007 The Mongol Art of War for the Mongol expansion; Mann 1986 The Sources of Social Power, Vol. 1 for the longue-durée imperial pattern; Liverani 1993 Akkad: The First World Empire for the Akkadian anchor
  - *Repeats.* Unique to Empire (sibling to Meat Pooling at Band, same Reactor class, opposed social logic)
- Empire-Human is the only symbolic-line cell to carry a secondary personality disorder panel in the framework, reflecting that the Universality motivation, when it fails, produces characteristic decompensation profiles not seen at earlier cells; this makes Empire-Human the implicit referent for much of clinical personality taxonomy. [Framework observation from *Inheritance Lines v3.0*; no extraction source]
- Stories (Planner capacity). At Empire-scale, identity becomes something you construct and project, not just inherit. Roman emperors built brands. Augustus reshaped his own name (from Octavian), his iconography, his civic narrative — the same image showed up on coins from Britain to Syria, in marble busts in every city, in the architecture of every forum. Paul Zanker traced the visual program: a deliberate, centrally directed brand campaign across an empire of fifty million people. Modern corporate branding runs on the same logic: Coca-Cola is recognizable in 200 countries with the same red and the same script. And Empire-Humans brand themselves — your name, your CV, your social media presence are tools you use to project a stable identity into contexts where strangers will encounter you and never meet you in person. The Stories capacity is strategic deliberation about how to be recognized at imperial scale.
  - *Citation.* Zanker 1988 The Power of Images in the Age of Augustus; Holland 2015 Dynasty on Roman imperial branding; Klein 1999 No Logo for the modern corporate parallel
  - *Repeats.* Unique to Empire
- Extracting (Pursuer capacity). Empire-Humans are masters of extraction. The Spanish discovered the Cerro Rico silver mountain at Potosí (modern Bolivia) in 1545 and ran mining operations there for nearly three centuries, forcing roughly 14,000 indigenous laborers a year into the mines through the mita corvée labor system. By 1600 Potosí was one of the largest cities in the world — its population entirely organized around extraction. The silver flowed to Seville and from there to Antwerp, Genoa, and ultimately to merchants buying tea and porcelain in Canton. Empires don't just take territory; they construct elaborate systems to pull resources out of conquered land and conquered people. Modern extractive industries — oil, lithium, cobalt, rare earths — run on the same template, with the legal forms updated but the structural logic preserved.
  - *Citation.* Bakewell 1984 Miners of the Red Mountain; Bauer 2001 Goods, Power, History: Latin America's Material Culture for the wider extractive system
  - *Repeats.* Unique to Empire
- Standardizing (Conservator capacity). When the first emperor of China, Qin Shi Huang, unified the warring states in 221 BCE, he ordered standardization across the new empire: the writing script (so a bureaucrat in any province could read documents from any other), the axle widths of carts (so wagons could use any road), the weights and measures, the currency. The point wasn't to invent these standards — most already existed locally — but to enforce a single standard across territories the size of modern France, populations who would never meet each other. The Roman parallel runs alongside it: standardized brick dimensions, road widths, Latin as administrative language, the libra as currency. Empires run on enforced uniformity. The City introduces standardization within a single urban core; the Empire scales it across populations who never meet, through enforcement infrastructures (inspectors, prefects, governors) that the City didn't need.
  - *Citation.* Lewis 2007 The Early Chinese Empires: Qin and Han; Bodde 1986 in Cambridge History of China Vol. 1 on Qin standardization
  - *Repeats.* Same capacity at City, different territorial scope. City case is the founding city-level metrology (shekel, cubit, brick); Empire case is imperial-scale uniformity enforced across vast territories (Qin script and measures, Roman uniform measures)

**Smithers coverage.** MODERATE for personality anchors. De Raad et al. (2010, 2014) confirmed HIGH in SQLite, providing the strongest empirical grounding for the Intellect (non-universal Openness) claim. Assmann (1995, 2011) confirmed HIGH in SQLite, grounding the Trust milestone in cultural memory theory. HEXACO literature (Ashton & Lee 2007; Ashton et al. 2014) at MODERATE provides the Integrity anchor. ABSENT for empire history, Axial Age scholarship (Jaspers, Bellah, Armstrong), social identity theory (Tajfel & Turner), and the imagined communities literature (Anderson, 1983) — all necessary for an empirically grounded Empire-Human book passage.

## Cross-cutting notes

### Big Five buildup across the symbolic line

| Slot | Band-Human | Settlement-Human | City-Human | Empire-Human |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Effector×Regulator Controller | Reputation | **Conscientiousness** *(debut)* | Conscientiousness | Conscientiousness |
| Regulator×Modeler Anticipator | Experiencing Style | Assertiveness | **Extraversion** *(debut)* | Extraversion |
| Modeler×Reviser Adapter | Agreeableness | Agreeableness | Righteousness | **Integrity** *(debut)* |
| Reviser×Effector Explorer | Neuroticism | Neuroticism | Neuroticism | **Intellect** *(debut, replaces Neuroticism)* |
| Effector∩Modeler Connector | Self-Reference | Self-Reference | **Self-Evaluation** *(debut)* | Self-Evaluation |
| Regulator∩Reviser Operator | Sociometer | **Self-Construal** *(debut)* | Self-Construal | **Identity** *(debut)* |

Openness-to-Experience has no structural slot on the symbolic line. Its psycholexical non-replication (De Raad et al., 2010, 2014) is consistent with its omission.

### Breakthrough progression

Speaking (Band) → Common Knowledge (Settlement) → Codes (City) → Trust (Empire)

Each breakthrough extends the radius of coordination: face-to-face band → multi-household village → anonymous city → imagined civilizational community.

### Symbiosis vs. elaboration

- **Band → Settlement:** elaboration (mobile band + storage = settled village)
- **Settlement → City:** symbiosis (settlements + trade networks = city)
- **City → Empire:** symbiosis (cities + colonial outposts = empire)

### Constituent-human type progression

Band-Human forager → Settlement-Human sedentary farmer → City-Human occupational-role urban dweller → Empire-Human imagined-community imperial subject

### Escalation items (surfaced before writing; not adjudicated here)

1. **Neanderthal symbolic evidence (resolved):** Band-Human is ecology-defined; Speaking is a capacity with contested horizon and species-spread; both the sapiens and Neanderthal records are presented, and the sapiens-specific versus genus-level question is left open by framework decision.
2. **Self-Reference cluster absent:** No Smithers extraction covers Cooley, Lewis, Tangney, Tracy & Robins, or Hofstadter — the cognitive infrastructure for Band-Human's Connector signature is entirely [INFERRED].
3. **Neolithic archaeology absent:** No extraction covers Çatalhöyük, Göbekli Tepe, or Fertile Crescent chronology — all Settlement-Human milestone material is [INFERRED].
4. **Axial Age absent:** No extraction covers Jaspers, Bellah, Armstrong, or Anderson — Empire-Human milestone material and imagined-communities logic are [INFERRED].

## Intellectual Kinships

This section records thinkers, traditions, and bodies of work that the framework absorbs or converges with at the symbolic line. Two patterns organize the entries. **Absorption** means the thinker's vocabulary enters the Venns directly as the canonical content for a specific region. **Convergence** means the thinker arrives at a compatible structural commitment by an independent route without shared vocabulary.

### Absorptions

**Harari.** Yuval Noah Harari. *Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind* (2011). Narrative collective identity as the mechanism by which large-scale human cooperation becomes possible across kin and tribal boundaries. ABHOP places Trust at the Empire breakthrough — the stranger-reliance Harari's narrative collective identity makes possible — and places Stories, that narrative-identity mechanism, at the Planner capacity that builds it; Harari's framing names what empires can do that lower symbolic cells cannot.

**Social Identity (Tajfel & Turner; Erikson; McAdams; Goffman).** Henri Tajfel and John Turner, social identity theory (1979 onward). Erik Erikson, identity-formation work (1950 onward). Dan McAdams, narrative identity. Erving Goffman, *The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life* (1959). ABHOP absorbs these as the primary anchors of Identity, the signature at the Empire-Human Regulator×Reviser pair, the Operator signature. Identity is the social-science synthesis of who the person takes themselves to be within a universalizing order. It couples Stability with Universality — the empire-level Operator signature.

**Jonathan Haidt.** Moral Foundations Theory (Haidt and Joseph, 2004 onward; *The Righteous Mind*, 2012). Six moral foundations (Care, Fairness, Loyalty, Authority, Sanctity, Liberty) as the cross-cultural foundation of moral cognition. ABHOP absorbs MFT at the Empire-Human Regulator×Reviser Operator signature, Identity. MFT operationalizes the universal moral codes empires encode. The Universality flavor of the six foundations is what places MFT at the Operator signature rather than the Connector signature at this level.

**Boyd & Richerson / Henrich.** Robert Boyd, Peter Richerson, Joseph Henrich. Dual inheritance theory. *Not by Genes Alone* (2005). Joseph Henrich's *The Secret of Our Success* (2015) and *The WEIRDest People in the World* (2020). Dual inheritance theory converges on ABHOP's line architecture: genetic plus symbolic plus a distinct cultural inheritance modality with its own selection dynamics. Henrich's WEIRD/kinship work enters the Empire-Stack treatment: monotheism dissolving clan loyalties, cousin-marriage bans, and individualism as a civilization-scale identity solution.

**Deacon (*Symbolic Species*).** Terrence Deacon. *The Symbolic Species* (1997). Pre-symbolic indexical and iconic reference and the symbolic transition. ABHOP absorbs Deacon's pre-symbolic reference work as the symbolic line's pre-cell semiotic groundwork, installed by the founding constellation before the Band-Human cell opens the culturally transmitted inheritance stream. Deacon's pre-biotic ratchets (*Incomplete Nature*, 2012) are absorbed separately at the Protocell; see `clade_reference_genetic` doc.

Tomasello (shared intentionality). Michael Tomasello. Shared-intentionality research program (Tomasello, Carpenter, Call, Behne & Moll, 2005; Why We Cooperate, 2009; A Natural History of Human Thinking, 2014). The capacity to form a shared "we" (joint goals, joint attention, and joint commitment) is what distinguishes human cooperation from the individual-intentionality social cognition of other great apes, which already manage competition, tactical deception, and alliance-tracking. ABHOP absorbs shared intentionality as the basis of Commitment, the Effector motivation at Band-Human: the we-mode is what lets non-kin bind themselves to common purpose, with language-tracked reputation as the enforcement layer that stabilizes it against defection. Tomasello's distinction between joint intentionality (dyadic) and collective intentionality (group-level, norm-governed) rhymes with the symbolic line's progression from Band to Empire. He is the boundary author for the neuronal-to-symbolic transition: he names what primate social cognition has and what it lacks.

**Codes (Goody and Scott).** Jack Goody, The Logic of Writing and the Organization of Society (1986); The Domestication of the Savage Mind (1977). James C. Scott, Seeing Like a State (1998); Against the Grain (2017). ABHOP anchors the Codes breakthrough on their account of written rule as the technology of large-scale coordination. Goody supplies the administrative reading: writing scales administration, law, and accounting past the reach of oral memory. Scott supplies the legibility reading: a state governs at scale by making its population legible through standardized records, and writing originates as a fiscal and accounting technology rather than a literary one. Together they name what Codes is and why it carries the City breakthrough, where the written, portable, enforceable record bears the coordination load that face-to-face settlement norms cannot. Scott's fiscal-origin claim grounds the cell's first-writing-is-Codes note. These anchors are pending verification and Smithers ingest.

### Convergences

**Pinker.** Steven Pinker. *The Better Angels of Our Nature* (2011) converges on the framework's symbolic-line developmental story: violence declines as the symbolic line builds increasingly comprehensive normative coordination structures from band to empire. *The Blank Slate* (2002) identifies three myths about human nature (Blank Slate, Noble Savage, Ghost in the Machine); ABHOP's fallacy taxonomy uses these three plus a fourth Pinker does not name (Dealt Hand). *The Language Instinct* (1994) converges on ABHOP's neuronal-line commitment to language as a biological substrate rather than a cultural overlay.

**Innis.** Harold Innis. Empire and Communications (1950); The Bias of Communication (1951). The medium that carries a code sets the reach of the polity that runs on it. Light portable media such as papyrus and paper carry a spatial bias and extend administration across wide territory. Durable media such as clay and stone carry a temporal bias and extend authority across time. Innis converges on the Codes breakthrough from the medium side: the form of the standing record bounds how large and how long-lived a coordinated order can be.

**North and Greif.** Douglass North, Institutions, Institutional Change and Economic Performance (1990); Avner Greif, Institutions and the Path to the Modern Economy (2006). Codified enforceable rules substitute for personal trust and enable the move from personal to impersonal exchange. Impersonal exchange is what lets markets grow beyond the circle of people who know each other. North and Greif converge on Codes as the institution that scales economic coordination among strangers.

**Hidalgo.** Cesar Hidalgo. Why Information Grows (2015). The know-how a network can hold bounds how complex and how large an economy can become. Hidalgo converges on the deepest form of the rhyme, the chain from information capacity to organizational scale, one line over from the genetic line's energy-to-information-to-complexity chain.

**West and Bettencourt.** Geoffrey West and Luis Bettencourt, with collaborators (Bettencourt, Lobo, Helbing, Kuhnert and West, PNAS 2007; Bettencourt, Science 2013). Cities scale like metabolizing organisms, with socioeconomic output rising superlinearly and infrastructure rising sublinearly with population. They converge on the cities-as-organisms reading and supply its quantitative form. Their causal lever is interaction density rather than codes, which leaves open the bridge the framework draws through the chimeric-merger reading.

None of these are yet covered by a Smithers extraction. Innis and the West-Bettencourt urban-scaling work are web-cited; the remainder are authorial lineage pending verification and Smithers ingest.

### The symbolic-line learning lineage

These thinkers ground two things the framework leans on at the symbolic line: how a learner like Bramble acquires language and motor control, and how language itself evolves as a population-level system, which is what the framework's super-organism reading and the Speaking-as-Natural-Selection rhyme rest on. They sit alongside the absorptions and convergences above as a distinct learning-and-evolution lineage.

**Cangelosi.** Angelo Cangelosi. Developmental and evolutionary robotics of language; *Simulating the Evolution of Language* (Cangelosi & Parisi, 2002); grounded language learning in robots. Cangelosi grounds the method by which Bramble acquires words: labels associated with multimodal sensory experience of a referent, learned by a robot rather than hand-coded. He bridges both roles, having modeled individual grounded acquisition and the emergence of communication in populations of agents.

**Steels.** Luc Steels. Language games and the Talking Heads experiment (1999 onward); language as a complex adaptive system. Steels grounds both the lab's method and the super-organism reading. His robots and agents negotiate a shared lexicon through repeated communicative games; conventions that succeed spread while the rest fall away, which is selection on linguistic variants for communicative fitness, language treated as an evolving population-level system rather than a fixed code in one head.

**Kirby.** Simon Kirby. Iterated learning; the cultural evolution of linguistic structure (Edinburgh, 2000s onward). Kirby grounds the claim that grammatical structure emerges through transmission rather than being fully specified in advance: a language passed through a learning bottleneck across generations adapts to be learnable, so compositionality emerges as a property of the transmitted system. This is selection for learnability across cultural generations, a population-level evolutionary dynamic on language.

**Taniguchi.** Tadahiro Taniguchi. Symbol emergence in robotics; the collective predictive coding hypothesis. Taniguchi is the most explicitly collective of the four: a symbol system is something a population infers and holds together, not a possession of any single agent. This is the closest existing model to the framework's super-organism reading of language, the collective as the unit that carries the symbolic system.

**Thelen and Adolph.** Esther Thelen and Karen Adolph. Dynamic-systems accounts of infant motor development; the crawl-to-walk transition and locomotor learning. They ground Bramble's motor bootstrapping curve. Infant locomotion develops through a stability-ordered sequence under continuous exploration rather than unfolding on a fixed schedule, which is why the new humanoid chassis climbs from crawling to running by control complexity rather than skipping ahead.

**Peirce.** Charles Sanders Peirce. Theory of signs; the icon/index/symbol trichotomy and the interpretant. The interpretant is the effect a sign produces in an interpreter, which makes Peirce's account a by-consequences theory of meaning: a sign's content is the practical difference it makes. ABHOP takes the interpretant as the fitness criterion for the meme. A spoken token is selected by the interpretant it produces, the way a gene is selected by survival and a neme by reward. Peirce is the author who makes all three lines selection by consequences: survival, reward, interpretant. [Framework-native synthesis: reading the interpretant as a Darwinian fitness criterion is the framework's move, not Peirce's; held as inference.]

**Shannon.** Claude Shannon. *A Mathematical Theory of Communication* (1948). Information as the reduction of uncertainty over a set of alternatives, measured in bits. ABHOP uses Shannon as the measure on the Speaking selector: each token is a selection over the lexicon, and the uncertainty it reduces is the formal score. Shannon supplies the meter, not the criterion. The uncertainty being reduced is the interpretant's, not the string's: the speaker minimizes referential and intentional uncertainty in a listener. Shannon already anchors the Modeler function in the framework's goo mapping; this is the same machinery applied at the symbolic selector.

**Chomsky.** Noam Chomsky. Generative grammar; structure-dependent rules. ABHOP uses Chomsky for the constraint on the candidate space: grammar defines which token sequences count as well-formed candidates, so the selection runs over a structured space rather than a flat lexicon. The framework takes only the thin commitment that token production is a constrained selection over a combinatorial symbolic space, and does not adjudicate strong nativism: Chomsky and Pinker hold rich innate grammar, Deacon holds that grammar adapts to brains through transmission. [The thin claim is well supported across these authors; the nativism question is left open.]

**The Szathmáry tie.** Eörs Szathmáry, with John Maynard Smith, *The Major Transitions in Evolution* (1995). The framework already cites Szathmáry through Watson and Szathmáry for evolution-as-learning at System 0. The major-transitions work treats language as a transition that opens a new system of heredity, which is the framework's reading of Speaking: the founding breakthrough that opens the symbolic inheritance system and serves as its selector. Token production is a selection over the lexicon, scored by the interpretant it achieves (Peirce), measured as uncertainty reduction (Shannon), and constrained to well-formed candidates by grammar (Chomsky, Pinker). Deacon's pre-symbolic reference supplies the combinatorial space the selection runs over. This grounds the Speaking-as-Natural-Selection rhyme: speaking is to the meme what natural selection is to the gene, each its line's selector. The super-organism trajectory across the symbolic line follows.

None of these nine are yet covered by a Smithers extraction; they are authorial lineage, pending-Smithers as cited anchors. The productive-morphology beat (coinage and overregularization as emergent rule-extraction) rests additionally on Berko's wug paradigm and the Rumelhart-McClelland connectionist account, in contrast with the innate-rule reading scoped to the neuronal substrate.
